designs.understanding: Every outbound call (four research sources, EPO auth, PatentsView, three model providers, and soon news feeds) is made ad hoc: research calls go through sources._get_json, which caches, checks a remembered pause, and then counts one request against a single settings.research_daily_limit (default 0, so no denominator) before calling client.get with no try. Its only output is (http_status, data), so 'our own cap', 'remembered 429 pause' and 'the source said 429' are all status 429, and papers()/paper_count() map every 429 to 'add OPENALEX_API_KEY'. A transport error (ReadTimeout, ConnectError) or a non-JSON 200 escapes as an exception through asyncio.gather in scan.py and novelty.py and kills the whole research job. PatentsView and the EPO token call bypass _get_json entirely (client.post), so they are neither counted nor protected. On the model side, s.usage is one flat dict that adds Ollama's local tokens to Gemini's, _budget_left stops every provider when the sum hits SESSION_TOKEN_BUDGET, nothing counts provider requests per minute or per day, and the panel fires seven seat calls at once with no limiter, so a burst from two founders trips Gemini's free-tier RPM and then the three-strikes breaker for five minutes for everyone. The research calls that could run in parallel (papers' three OpenAlex requests, element rows, novelty context and retarget) run serially, and the ones that do run in parallel have no per-source concurrency cap. One root cause: there is no single outbound gate that owns, per source or provider, the limit and its window, the concurrency, the pause, the failure reason and the counters.

flags_disputed.note: Evidence holds, but SESSION_TOKEN_BUDGET defaults to 0 (config.py:53), so the Ollama over-count only bites when an owner sets a budget. The missing per-provider daily count is the larger half of the flag.

Holds; the 'counts refused requests' point is correct: _over_budget INCRs before deciding, so 'used' keeps rising after the cap.

approaches.name: Single outbound gate module (core/outbound.py) with a per-source limit table, per-source semaphores, an outcome enum and Redis/local counters
approaches.how: Every external call (research sources, EPO auth, PatentsView, model providers, news feeds) goes through gate.call(source, send). The gate checks the remembered pause, checks and counts the source's rate windows (minute/day) only for requests actually sent, holds a per-source asyncio.Semaphore while the request runs, catches transport and decode errors, and returns a typed Outcome (ok, capped, paused, upstream_limited, transport_error, http_error, bad_response). Counters use the existing Redis INCR+EXPIRE pattern with an in-process fallback.
approaches.basis: Generalises code that already exists (_paused, _pause, _over_budget, Breaker) into one place; standard library asyncio plus the redis client already installed; the same fixed-window pattern as Flask-Limiter
approaches.advantages: One place fixes every symptom: per-source denominators for the 80% rule, true reasons, isolation of failures, bounded bursts, and one snapshot for the 5.4.3 page. No new dependency; key names stay budget:{source}:{window}.
approaches.drawbacks: Per-process semaphores do not bound several workers (Redis counters still do); limits are hand-entered from provider pages and can drift.

approaches.name: limits library (fixed/moving windows with Redis storage) plus aiolimiter for bursts
approaches.how: Use the 'limits' package for per-source windows with its async Redis backend, and aiolimiter leaky buckets for per-minute smoothing.
approaches.basis: Mature libraries (limits underpins slowapi and Flask-Limiter; aiolimiter is the common asyncio limiter)
approaches.advantages: Tested window algorithms, a ready 'remaining' query.
approaches.drawbacks: Two new dependencies for a few counters; a second Redis key scheme next to budget:{source}:{date} in SYSTEM-DESIGN and the runbook; still needs our own outcome enum, error isolation and usage split, which are most of the work.

approaches.name: Read provider rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining/Reset, Retry-After) as the budget source
approaches.how: Store the remaining/reset values each response carries and refuse calls when remaining reaches zero.
approaches.basis: GitHub sends these headers on every search; OpenAlex and Gemini send Retry-After on 429
approaches.advantages: The true remaining budget, no hand-entered numbers.
approaches.drawbacks: OpenAlex, ClinicalTrials.gov and EPO do not send remaining counts, so it cannot be the whole answer; it says nothing about failure isolation, reasons or token budgets.

approaches.name: Per-call-site fixes: gather(return_exceptions=True) in scan/novelty, a reason string in _get_json, a provider key in s.usage, a semaphore in council
approaches.how: Patch each symptom where it shows: five gather sites, the two 429 branches, the usage dict, the seat fan-out.
approaches.advantages: Each change is tiny and local.
approaches.drawbacks: No owner for limits or concurrency: PatentsView, EPO auth and the coming news fetcher would each need the same fixes again; the 80% alert still has no shared denominator; easy to miss a call site (two are already missed).

approaches.name: Redis-backed queue with dedicated workers (arq / RQ / Celery) that serialises outbound work
approaches.how: Move research and panel jobs onto a Redis queue; worker concurrency becomes the rate limit.
approaches.basis: arq is a small asyncio Redis queue; Celery and RQ are the mainstream Python task queues
approaches.advantages: Shared across processes; natural place for retries and priorities.
approaches.drawbacks: Redis must stay optional (offline baseline), so an in-process path is needed anyway; a queue is the 2.3.1/SYSTEM-DESIGN §7 scaling step, not a rate-limit design; heavy for one small team now.

approaches.name: Prometheus client counters plus alert rules
approaches.how: Count outbound requests and tokens with prometheus_client and alert at 80% in Prometheus.
approaches.advantages: Labels per provider, a standard exposition format.
approaches.drawbacks: Needs a Prometheus server to aggregate and alert, which the free no-hosting setup does not have; it observes limits but enforces none.

It fixes all seven flags with one mechanism, reuses code and key names already in sources.py and services/breaker.py, needs no dependency, works with Redis off (local counters) and keeps the founder-facing SourceResult.status contract while adding the operator-facing reason. Reading GitHub's X-RateLimit-Remaining inside the gate costs a few lines and makes the GitHub percentage exact without depending on headers for sources that do not send them.

design.components: 1) core/outbound.py: SourcePolicy (name, windows, concurrency, metered), Outcome enum, Gate with async call(), snapshot(); 2) research/sources.py: _get_json becomes a thin wrapper over gate.call that keeps the cache in front (T08 owns the cache); every connector including PatentsView and EPO auth goes through it; SourceResult gains a `reason` field; 3) agents/providers.py: each provider call goes through the gate under source 'model:<name>', with Provider.metered (False for Ollama); usage recorded per provider; 4) agents/jobs.py: per-kind concurrency (research, council) inside Board.run; 5) research/scan.py and novelty.py: independent calls gathered, with the gate's semaphores bounding the burst; 6) a read-only outbound snapshot for the 5.4.3 monitoring page (T23).
design.data_model: Settings: outbound_limits: dict[str, str] parsed from OUTBOUND_LIMITS='openalex=day:0;github=minute:10;epo=minute:10;model:gemini=minute:0,day:0', where 0 means 'count only, no limit known' (never an invented number; the shipped defaults are only the limits the code already documents: GitHub unauthenticated search 10/min, EPO about 10 searches/min), and outbound_concurrency: dict[str,int] (default 4 per research source, 1 for epo, 3 for model:gemini, 1 for model:ollama). research_daily_limit stays as a deprecated alias that fills day:N for every research source. Outcome = StrEnum(ok, cached, capped, paused, upstream_limited, transport_error, http_error, bad_response, no_key). GateResult(outcome, status:int|None, data, retry_at:float|None). SourceResult adds reason: str (an Outcome value) beside status. Redis keys: budget:{source}:{window}:{bucket} (bucket = UTC date or minute index) with EXPIRE of two windows; rs:neg:{source} kept for pauses. Session usage becomes {'by_provider': {'gemini': {'input_tokens','output_tokens','requests'}, 'ollama': {...}}} with a reader that accepts the old flat dict (T34 owns the document version bump).
design.algorithm: gate.call(source, send): if paused(source) -> GateResult(paused). For each window of the policy: read the counter; if limit>0 and used>=limit -> capped (nothing is incremented for refused calls). Acquire the per-source semaphore; INCR each window counter; await send() inside try: httpx.TransportError -> transport_error; JSON/ValueError -> bad_response; 429 (and 403 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 for GitHub) -> pause until Retry-After or the reset header, upstream_limited; other non-2xx -> http_error(status); 2xx -> ok. Record the outcome in a per-source daily counter (outcome:{source}:{date}) for the dashboard. Mapping to SourceResult: ok->ok; capped->budget_exhausted with note 'Vanigam's own limit for <source> reached; resets <time>'; paused->budget_exhausted 'asked us to wait until <time>'; upstream_limited->budget_exhausted with the key hint only when no key is configured; transport_error/http_error/bad_response->error. Models: seat calls use gate.call('model:gemini', ..., priority='bulk'); bulk callers are refused (capped) when the minute window has fewer than reserve (default 2) left, so live turns keep headroom; seats refused by the gate fall back to the rule seat with reason 'rate', and a gate refusal is NOT a Breaker.fail (no call was made). _spent sums only metered providers. Parallelism: papers() gathers its three OpenAlex requests; scan gathers element rows; novelty gathers context and retarget; _research_work runs scan and novelty's part/pair counts concurrently and joins for the context step. Board: asyncio.Semaphore per kind (research 4, council 2 by default) acquired inside run(), so a queued job is RUNNING to wait() and the turn simply narrates 'still looking'.
design.interfaces: T08 (cache semantics): the cache stays in front of the gate; a non-ok outcome is never cached; T08's credential-free cache key is used unchanged. T12 (bounded in-process state): Board semaphores and per-source state are dicts keyed by a fixed source list. T23 (observability): gate.snapshot() -> {source: {windows:[{window, used, limit, pct}], paused_until, outcomes_today}} feeds 5.4.2.2/5.4.3; pct is null when limit is 0. T21 (news): the news refresher calls the gate with source 'news:<id>' and an hourly window. T34 (session format): the usage shape change rides the document version field. T25 (egress): private mode is checked before the gate is reached, as today.
design.rollout: 1) Land the gate with isolation and the outcome enum behind existing settings (research_daily_limit mapped into day windows), so behaviour is unchanged except that one failing source no longer fails the scan. 2) Switch connectors and the 429 notes to reasons; update the runbook table of reasons -> actions. 3) Add parallel calls once per-source semaphores are in place. 4) Route model providers and the panel through the gate; split usage per provider with a backward-compatible reader. 5) Expose the snapshot to the monitoring work.
design.offline: Redis off: counters and pauses live in process (as today). Network off: every call ends as transport_error, each source reports 'not searched this time', and the conversation continues on local data and the rule path. Ollama is unmetered, so a founder on the local model never hits the session token budget.

designs.understanding: The Alembic chain is not a frozen history. 0001 imports app.models.Base and runs metadata.create_all for four tables, so its result changes whenever a model changes, and the first later add_column migration on founders or startups (3.1.2, T30) fails with DuplicateColumn on a fresh database. 0003 imports pgvector and runs CREATE EXTENSION vector for an embeddings table that no code reads and whose feature is Dropped, and 0004 (agent_sessions, the table the product needs) sits after it, so 'alembic upgrade head' fails on the owner's stock PostgreSQL 18 and on any stock CI image. The only integration tests build tables with Base.metadata.create_all on the developer database and turn every setup error into a skip, so the migrations are never exercised and a schema error looks like 'no database'. CI has no database step and no drift check. documents, embeddings and models/schemas.py are dead; founders/startups are unused, but users.founder_id references founders, and T30 will reshape them.

design.algorithm: Owner rule: allow when s.owner_id is None, or user is not None and str(user.user_id) == s.owner_id; otherwise 404 'Session not found' (never 403, so a probe cannot confirm existence). Claim: UPDATE agent_sessions SET owner_id=:u, data = jsonb_set(data,'{owner_id}',to_jsonb(:u::text)), version=version+1 WHERE session_id = ANY(:ids) AND owner_id IS NULL RETURNING session_id; claim ignores the six-hour idle hide (it reads rows directly) but respects retention (T07/T32). The browser sends its recent-session list (T18) after sign-in only when the founder confirms 'Keep these conversations in your account?' with each title shown, so a second person on a shared phone sees what they would be taking. Listing: SELECT session_id, idea_version, last_active, private and the idea slot via a JSONB expression FROM agent_sessions WHERE owner_id=:u ORDER BY last_active DESC LIMIT 50 (no document parse).

designs.understanding: Seven vanigam_* keys are written directly with localStorage by six modules, each with its own shape, versioning rule and error handling. Two (journeyStore.ts and pages/Journey.tsx) use the same key 'vanigam_journey' with different shapes: whichever writes last destroys the other's data, and Journey crashes reading facts.district from the other shape. journeyStore discards any record whose version differs instead of migrating. Logout only removes tokens, so the next person on a shared device inherits profile (including caste and phone), journey consent, pipeline, supplier quotes and the Talk session, and any future sign-in sync would upload them into the wrong account. Talk keeps one session id and deletes it on any resume error (network, 500, 503, 404 alike), losing the only handle to a conversation that still exists, including the handle needed to delete it. Lists use Date.now() ids and whole-array writes, so the planned server sync (3.1.3) has no merge rule. Root cause: no storage layer that owns keys, scope (device vs founder), versions and migrations, and no typed error policy in the session client.

design.data_model: Physical key 'vanigam.<owner>.<name>' for founder scope (owner = 'anon' or user_id), 'vanigam.<name>' for device scope; value = {v: version, data}. Legacy keys (vanigam_profile, vanigam_journey, vanigam_pipeline, vanigam_suppliers, vanigam_talk_session) migrate once into the anon namespace; vanigam_journey is sniffed (version 1 -> journeyStore v1; facts/done -> registration) and both merge into v2. talk.sessions: [{id, started_at, title|null, last_seen}] max 10. Sync contract for 3.1.3: each record {version, items: [{id: uuid, updated_at, deleted_at|null, ...}]}; PUT with If-Match version -> 409 on conflict; first sync = union by id, newer updated_at wins per item, tombstones win over older edits.
design.algorithm: Migration runner: missing -> default; v < current -> apply migrate[v..current-1] in order; v > current (a newer client wrote it) -> leave it untouched and use the default in memory without writing; unparseable -> copy raw to '<key>.unreadable' once, then default. Adopt: only when the anonymous namespace holds founder data and the founder confirms; profile/journey merge prefers the user's existing values; lists union by id. Sign-out: unsynced = items updated after the last successful sync (before 3.1.3 everything is local, so the dialog says 'only on this device'); the default action removes the namespace.
design.interfaces: T17: the claim endpoint takes talk.sessions ids after the adopt confirmation; my-conversations replaces the single id when signed in. T07: provides the 404 vs 410 distinction on resume. T19: the journey consent field takes the purpose-keyed shape from the registry. T20: cohort.enrolments holds programme enrolment tokens. T14: tokens stay device scope; 401 handling. T21: Intel reads founder context through this module. 3.1.2/3.1.3 server sync implements the contract above.

designs.understanding: POST /cohort/programme aggregates whatever list of up to 500 session ids the caller sends. Because the caller chooses the set, adding one target id to four or five known or self-made consenting sessions reveals the target's consent, district, sector, stage, capital band, novelty type and panel band by differencing; the minimum-5 fold does not resist set differences. Some outputs bypass the fold entirely (founders_sharing exact, reached_a_roadmap 1-4, an exact average progress). The floor counts sessions, not founders, so restarted sessions of one person inflate it. The ids the programme pastes are full read/write/delete keys to the conversations (T17). The endpoint has no auth, and the planned auth needs the users table, which is blocked. Sessions idle over six hours are also silently dropped from the aggregate because it reads through store.get. Root cause: no server-owned membership and no single disclosure-control function that every output passes through.

designs.understanding: The news board calls fetcher.fetch() on every request and ranks whatever comes back. Today the only working fetcher is the fixture corpus; HttpNewsFetcher raises. rank() indexes BY_ID[art.source_id] during dedupe before its own attribution guard, so one unknown source crashes the board. RawArticle.published is documented as ISO but nothing enforces it, and _days_old returns 999 for anything else, so RSS RFC 822 dates would rank as stale. Actionability is a substring match ('funding', 'apply', 'launch'), so funding-round news and closed calls get 'something to act on'. The redirect guard checks all listed domains (not just fetchable ones) and ignores the scheme; robots_ok is a static flag. Intel labels fixtures 'cached', sends no founder context, and rank() ignores language. A minor extra: the sort tie-break uses published ascending, so older items win ties. Root cause: no stored corpus with a defined ingest boundary (normalised, attributed, policy-checked items), and keyword-only item typing.

flags_disputed.note: Holds; the flag's line numbers are stale (pipeline.py is now 223 lines), but the BY_ID[...] lookups inside the dedupe loop still precede the BY_ID.get guard.

Every item passes ingest(): drop unattributable, normalise published to ISO (RFC 822 via email.utils, ISO via fromisoformat, else 'date unknown'), clamp the extract. rank() types each item as call / closed / funding_news / other with phrase lists and a deadline-date reader.

approaches.drawbacks: Needs the scheduler (T32/5.4.4); phrase lists need upkeep, including Tamil phrases reviewed by a Tamil reader.

design.components: 1) news/ingest.py: ingest(raw) -> RawArticle | None: drop if source_id not in BY_ID; published -> ISO date or None ('date unknown') via date.fromisoformat / datetime.fromisoformat / email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime; clamp the extract (_clamp moves here). 2) news/corpus.py: CorpusStore.read()/write() on settings.news_corpus_file (resolved against the package dir, as 5.4.4.2 requires) with a Redis copy; keeps items up to 60 days. 3) news/refresh.py: for each fetchable source: robots check (urllib.robotparser, re-read daily); conditional GET with stored ETag/Last-Modified through the T15 gate (source 'news:<id>', hourly window); redirects followed manually up to 3 hops with is_fetchable_url (https and host in fetchable_sources()) after each; parse (feedparser inside HttpNewsFetcher once written); ingest; merge by item_id. One failing source records its status and keeps its old items. 4) pipeline.rank(): ingest guard first; classify(): kind in {call, closed, funding_news, other} from phrase lists (call: 'apply by', 'last date', 'applications open', 'invites applications', 'deadline', Tamil 'விண்ணப்பிக்க', 'கடைசி நாள்'; closed: 'closed', 'ended', 'results announced'; funding_news: 'raises', 'raised', 'secures', 'series [a-e]', 'funding round'). A deadline reader extracts dates near call phrases ('20 September', 'September 20, 2026', '20/09/2026', '20.09.2026', Tamil month names); latest deadline < today -> closed. Only 'call' gets 'something to act on' (with 'check the deadline' when no date was read); unknown date -> recency 0, reason 'date unknown', never act-on. Language boost +0.10 when article.language == ctx.language (no filter). Tie-break newest first. 5) routers/news.py reads the corpus; when no source is fetchable it serves fixtures with provider 'fixture'; the response gains corpus_refreshed_at and per-source status. 6) Intel.tsx: 'demo' when provider is fixture, 'updated <time>' from corpus_refreshed_at, 'stale' after 24 h; sends sector, district and stage from the founder's journey/profile (non-protected fields only) and the UI language.
design.data_model: corpus.json: {refreshed_at, sources: {id: {etag, last_modified, robots_checked_at, robots_allowed, last_status, last_ok_at}}, items: [RawArticle as dict with published ISO|null]}. RawArticle.published: str | None. NewsItem gains kind and deadline (ISO|null). NewsBoardOut gains corpus_refreshed_at and source_status.
design.algorithm: See components 3 and 4. Ranking weights are unchanged except actionability: 1.0 for an open call with a future deadline, 0.6 for an open call with no date read, 0 otherwise.
design.interfaces: T15: the refresher calls through the outbound gate (limits, pause, isolation, counters). T32/5.4.4: the scheduled runner calls news.refresh every few hours under its run lock. T18: Intel reads founder context through the storage module. T23: per-source status feeds the monitoring page. D9 decides whether fixtures are ever shown once a source is live; this design supports both answers.
design.rollout: 1) Ingest guard, date normalisation and the tie-break fix (works on fixtures today). 2) Item typing and the deadline reader. 3) Intel label, context and language boost. 4) Corpus store, refresher and strict guard, ready for the first verified source after D9 and 4.4.1.2; feedparser added in that PR.
design.offline: The board serves the last stored corpus (labelled with its age) or the fixture demo (labelled demo); no request ever waits on a publisher.

designs.tests: Unit: rank() with an item from source 'unknown' and a near-duplicate -> no exception, unknown item absent; 'Fri, 17 Oct 2026 08:00:00 GMT' -> 2026-10-17 and the '48 hours' reason; 'raises Rs 50 crore in Series B funding' -> funding_news, no act reason; 'Applications for TANSEED closed on 20 September' -> closed; 'apply by 30 November 2026' with today 2026-10-17 -> call, actionable; language boost reorders equal items; tie-break newest first. Refresher with httpx.MockTransport: 304 keeps items; a redirect to a listed but not fetchable host -> refused; an http:// redirect refused; robots disallow -> source skipped with status; one source timing out keeps the others. Router: with no fetchable source the response says provider fixture and Intel shows 'demo'.
designs.risks: Phrase lists miss unusual wording (false negatives are safer than a false 'act on'); the stdlib robots parser lacks some wildcard extensions (switch to protego only if a listed source needs it). The refresher depends on the scheduler from T32/5.4.4; until then the corpus can be refreshed by running the script by hand.
